questions.question: On a coordinate grid, Owen plots four points from his pattern: (1, 4), (2, 8), (3, 12) and (4, 16). Which rule matches every point he plotted?
options: y = 4x
y = x + 3
y = x + 4
questions.explain: A rule has to work for every point, not just the first one: 4 x 1 = 4, 4 x 2 = 8, 4 x 3 = 12, 4 x 4 = 16, so y = 4x. The common trap is checking only (1, 4), where adding 3 also seems to work but fails at (2, 8).

questions.question: On a coordinate grid, Leah plots the points (1, 5), (2, 7), (3, 9) and (4, 11). Which rule matches all four points?
options: y = 2x
y = 5x
questions.explain: The y-values go up by 2 each time x goes up by 1, so the rule multiplies x by 2, and 2 x 1 = 2 needs 3 more to reach 5, giving y = 2x + 3. The trap is swapping the step and the starting extra and writing 3x + 2, which gives 8 instead of 7 at x = 2.

questions.question: On a coordinate grid, Diego plots the points (0, 6), (1, 5), (2, 4) and (3, 3). Which sentence best explains the relationship between x and y?
options: y is always 6 less than x, so y = x - 6
Each time x increases by 1, y decreases by 2, so y = 6 - 2x
Each time x increases by 1, y decreases by 1, and y starts at 6, so y = 6 - x
Each time x increases by 1, y increases by 1, so y = x + 6
questions.explain: Read the change first: from 6 to 5 to 4 to 3 the y-value drops by 1 for each step of x, and it starts at 6, so y = 6 - x. A common trap is flipping the subtraction into y = x - 6, which would give a negative value at x = 1.

questions.question: On a coordinate grid, Amrit plots the points (1, 3), (2, 6), (3, 9) and (4, 12). Which statement correctly explains how y is related to x?
options: The points go up by 3 each step, so y = x + 3
x is always 3 times y, so x = 3y
y is always 2 more than x, so y = x + 2
y is always 3 times x, so each time x goes up by 1, y goes up by 3
questions.explain: Compare each y with its own x: 3 = 3 x 1, 6 = 3 x 2, 9 = 3 x 3, so y is 3 times x. The trap is turning the step of 3 into y = x + 3, which gives 5 at x = 2 instead of 6.

questions.question: A table of values shows n = 1, 2, 3, 4 in the top row and c = 5, 8, 11, 14 in the bottom row. Which expression gives c for every value of n?
options: 5n
3n
questions.explain: The c-values rise by 3 each time n rises by 1, and 3 x 1 = 3 is 2 short of 5, so c = 3n + 2. Test more than one row: 2n + 3 also gives 5 at n = 1 but gives 7 instead of 8 at n = 2.

questions.question: Ella graphs her savings. Her points are (0, 2), (1, 5), (2, 8) and (3, 11), where x is the number of weeks and y is dollars saved. She wants to know her savings after 10 weeks. Which reasoning is correct?
options: Multiply 10 by 5, giving $50, because the point (1, 5) is on the graph
She started with $2 and adds $3 each week, so 3 x 10 + 2 = $32
Multiply 10 by 3, giving $30, because y goes up by 3 each week
Multiply 10 by 2 and add 3, giving $23, because the start is 2 and the step is 3
questions.explain: Read two things off the graph: the starting amount at x = 0 (which is $2) and the change per week (which is $3), giving y = 3x + 2, so 10 weeks gives $32. The most common trap is forgetting the $2 she already had and answering $30.

questions.question: Sam graphs the water in his rain barrel as it drains. The points are (0, 40), (1, 37), (2, 34) and (3, 31), where x is minutes and y is litres. Which statement explains the relationship?
options: The barrel gains 3 L each minute, so y = 40 + 3x
The barrel starts with 37 L and loses 3 L each minute, so y = 37 - 3x
The barrel starts with 40 L and loses 3 L each minute, so y = 40 - 3x
The barrel loses 3 L in total over the whole time, so y = 40 - 3
questions.explain: The amount at x = 0 is the starting value of 40 L, and each minute the water drops by 3 L, so y = 40 - 3x. A common trap is reading the starting value from the point (1, 37) instead of from x = 0.

questions.question: Jae writes the rule y = 4x - 1 for a pattern. Which table of values matches Jae's rule?
questions.explain: Substitute each x into the rule: 4 x 1 - 1 = 3, 4 x 2 - 1 = 7, 4 x 3 - 1 = 11. The usual trap is multiplying by 4 and forgetting to subtract 1, which gives 4, 8, 12.

questions.question: A table shows x = 1, 2, 3, 4 with y = 5, 8, 11, 14. Priya says the rule is y = 5x because the first point on her graph is (1, 5). What is the best explanation of her mistake?
options: A rule must work for every pair, and y = 5x gives 10 when x = 2 instead of 8; the correct rule is y = 3x + 2
She should have used the last pair instead of the first, because it is the furthest along, so the rule is y = 14x
Her rule is fine for a table, but a graph needs the step of 3 instead, so on a graph the rule is y = 3x
She mixed up x and y, since the bigger number goes first, so the correct rule is x = 5y and her graph is flipped
questions.explain: One matching pair never proves a rule; test it on every row, and y = 5x fails at x = 2. Here y climbs by 3 each step and sits 2 above 3x, so y = 3x + 2 works for all four pairs.

questions.question: Malia graphs the cost of skating. Her points are (1, 6), (2, 8) and (3, 10), where x is hours and y is dollars. The rink charges a fixed entry fee plus an hourly rate. Malia has exactly $18 to spend. Which reasoning finds the number of hours correctly?
options: Each hour costs $2 and there is nothing else to pay, so 18 / 2 = 9 hours uses the money exactly
The cost rises $2 per hour, so the entry fee is 6 - 2 = $4; then 18 - 4 = 14 and 14 / 2 = 7 hours
One hour costs $6, as the first point (1, 6) shows, so 18 / 6 = 3 hours is what $18 will buy
Add the $4 entry fee to the $18, since the fee counts as money too, then 22 / 2 gives 11 hours
questions.explain: From the graph the cost goes up $2 per hour, so the $6 for one hour is $4 entry plus $2 skating; take the entry fee off first, then divide: (18 - 4) / 2 = 7 hours. The big trap is dividing the whole $18 by the hourly rate and forgetting the fixed fee.

questions.question: At the community pool, Plan A costs a $10 membership plus $3 for each swim, and Plan B costs $5 for each swim with no membership. Which statement about the two plans is true?
options: Plan B is always cheaper because it has no membership fee
Plan A is always cheaper because it goes up by only $3 for each swim
At 5 swims both plans cost $25, and after 5 swims Plan A costs less
At 2 swims the plans cost the same, $16 each
questions.explain: Write both rules and compare: Plan A is 3n + 10 and Plan B is 5n, and they meet at n = 5 where both equal $25, after which Plan A grows more slowly. The trap is judging by the step size or the membership fee alone; a smaller step does not make a plan cheaper until enough swims have passed.

questions.question: On one coordinate grid, Line P passes through (0, 1), (1, 5) and (2, 9). Line Q passes through (0, 6), (1, 8) and (2, 10). Jaya says Line Q grows faster because its points are higher up on the grid. Which explanation is correct?
options: Jaya is right, because 6 is greater than 1, so Q starts ahead and must be growing faster too
Jaya is wrong: Q rises 2 for each step while P rises 5, the y-value at x = 1, so P grows faster
Both lines grow at the same rate, because both sets of points lie in a straight line on the grid
Jaya is wrong: P rises 4 for each step while Q rises 2, so P grows faster and Q only starts higher
questions.explain: Growth is about the change from one point to the next, not how high the points sit: P goes 1, 5, 9 (up 4 each step) and Q goes 6, 8, 10 (up 2 each step). Careful with the step for P, it is 5 - 1 = 4, not the y-value 5 itself.
